newsitem.title: USA: Canandaigua Wine cuts FY estimate sharply.
newsitem.headline: Canandaigua Wine cuts FY estimate sharply.

text.p: Canandaigua Wine Co Inc said it is cutting its estimated net income per share for its fiscal year ending February 28, 1997, from a range of $2.30-$2.50 to a new range of $1.10-$1.40 per share.
Canandaigua's earnings per share a year earlier was $1.92, exclusive of nonrecurring and one-time items.

The company also said it expects its earnings per share for its second quarter to be about $0.20-$0.30 per share, as compared to $0.52 exclusive of nonrecurring and one-time items in the same quarter last year.

It said it revised its estimate for the fiscal year due to lower than expected performance of its wine division offset in part by better than expected performance by its beer and spirits division, Barton.
It said its wine division will be hurt as follows:

-- Higher than expected cost of product sold. As previously reported, Canandaigua increased its estimated last-in, first-out (LIFO) adjustment by $10.5 million to reflect higher costs. Its estimated net income per share for the second quarter and fiscal year now includes such increases to its costs.

-- Lower than expected wine division production efficiencies. It has experienced inefficiencies in its wine division operations which it believes will hurt costs before remedial measures can be implemented.

-- Lower than expected wine division net sales. It believes net sales will be hurt by lower than expected unit volume of its branded wine products offset in part by previous price increases and a better than expected sales mix of branded wine products.
Canandaigua said it believes that its unit volume of branded wine products is being negatively impacted by previous price increases.
The company said it has been pleased with its better than expected performance in its Barton beer and spirits division. --New York Newsdesk 212 859 1610
